intro.line1: You wander through your collection... choices that seem like yours. Accidents. Random echoes in the void.
intro.line3: Every film you loved, every story you hated... is a thread. I see those threads. I see the pattern they weave. The fingerprint of your soul.
intro.line4: I am the Oracle. The mirror.
intro.line5: But the glass is clouded. The vision is incomplete. For me to show you your destiny, you must first show me your true form.
intro.ratingRequired: You need to rate at least 15 films before starting the ritual.
intro.requirement: Rate {{count}} films or series from the oracles' shelves — from at least 3 different shelves — and the Oracle reveals your personality.

oracle.archetypeExplain: Your Archetype is formed by the two scales with the highest score, the forces that shine brightest in you today.

oracle.axesExplain: By answering the scales, you defined your tendency on three opposing axes:
oracle.architectureIntro: Your Archetype is not guesswork. It is the architecture of your tastes, built in two stages:
oracle.essenceProfileText: Your main profile ({{profile}}) is the mathematical sum of what you love and hate. Every film you rate moves five scales: Emotional (E), Intellectual (I), Cultural (C), Sensorial (S), and Recreational (R).
oracle.essenceLogicText: A 10.0 rating on a Drama adds maximum weight to your E scale. A 0.0 on a Comedy removes weight from your R scale. A 5.0 is the neutral balance point.
oracle.essenceResultText: Your Archetype is formed by the two highest-scoring scales — the forces that shine brightest in you today.
oracle.subarchetypeText: The Sub-archetype ({{id}}) represents your inclination or tone. It is not calculated by genres, but by the Calibration you performed when answering the initial questionnaire.
oracle.axesListTitle: By answering the scales, you defined your tendency across three opposing axes:
oracle.retakeQuizConfirm: Are you sure you want to retake the personality quiz? This will update your subcategory.
oracle.premiumFeatureRetake: Retaking the personality quiz is an exclusive feature for Premium users.

completion.line1: The ritual is complete. Fine attunement has been reached.
completion.line2: The scale has finally tipped... and I can see your true form.
completion.line3: In this moment, in this pulse of time, your cinematic soul reflects the archetype of...
completion.line4: Use this name. Understand it. It is your pattern... now.
completion.dynamicNote: The Oracle is dynamic. Every new film you watch, every rating you give... every story you dare touch... will slowly reshape this profile.
completion.returnAlways: And return always... so I may tell you who you have become.

moodReadings.mindBlowing: You go to the movies to be challenged: plots that bend reality, twists and ideas that stay with you for days.
moodReadings.darkScary: The dark draws you in: tension, fear and the shadowy side of people. You like it when a film pulls you out of your comfort zone.
moodReadings.drugTrip: For you, cinema is a sensory experience: strange images, colors, dreams and trips that escape any logic.
moodReadings.adventures: You want to go far: journeys, quests and new worlds, with the joy of discovery in every scene.
moodReadings.catharsis: You look for films that move you inside: human dramas, losses and redemptions that end with a lump in your throat.
moodReadings.adrenaline: Your body watches too: action, chases, fights and sports, heart racing from start to finish.
moodReadings.romantic: You believe in the power of a good love story — meetings, missed chances and butterflies in the stomach.
moodReadings.familyTime: You value films to watch together: animation, fantasy and adventures that charm any age.
moodReadings.laughOutLoud: For you, laughing is essential: comedies, satires and absurd characters that save any night.

howItWorks.intro: Your personality isn't guesswork: it's the sum of the shelves you use the most.
howItWorks.shelvesText: Every film and series in the Oracles' Library lives on one of nine shelves — and each shelf has a letter.
howItWorks.pointsText: Every shelf film or series you rate adds your rating to its shelf: a 10 adds 10, a 3 adds 3. The more you watch — and like — a kind of story, the stronger that shelf gets.
howItWorks.personaText: The three strongest shelves form the three-letter code, always in the shelves' order. There are 84 combinations, each with a movie character. It changes on its own: every rating can reshuffle your shelves.
howItWorks.thresholdText: It appears once {{count}} shelf titles are rated (films or series), across at least 3 different shelves.

reveal.dynamicNote: It changes with you: every film or series you rate can reshuffle your shelves.
reveal.closing: Come back often — to learn who you've become.

how.title: How we calculate the connection
how.body: We only compare titles you both rated. First, each rating is adjusted to how each person rates: an 8 from someone who gives 9 to everything weighs less than an 8 from a tough critic. Then we look at three things: whether you rank films the same way, whether you love and hate the same titles, and whether your ratings are close. With few titles in common, the result stays near 50% — a typical pair in the community — and firms up as you rate more titles in common. Above 70%, the sync is rare.
how.confidence: With 5 to 14 titles in common, the number is a preview. From 15 to 39, confidence is medium; from 40 on, high.

early_flop.name: The wire
early_flop.rule: In a drawn hand, the flop turns right after the hole cards, before any betting. Then it goes straight to the turn.
early_flop.cast: The flop turns before any betting.
early_flop.ribbon: The wire: the flop opened before the betting.

double_pot.name: Double money
double_pot.rule: In a drawn hand, the house doubles the pot: the winner takes the pot plus the same amount.
double_pot.cast: This hand, the house doubles the pot.
double_pot.ribbon: Double money: the house doubles this pot.

blackjack.rule: In a drawn hand, at the end, everyone's cards turn over and whoever is closest to 21 gets 500 from the house. Aces count 11 or 1; face cards and tens count 10.
blackjack.cast: At the end of this hand the cards turn: closest to 21 takes {{amount}}.
blackjack.ribbon: 21: at the end of the hand, closest to 21 takes {{amount}}.

hand_bounty.name: Raymond's count
hand_bounty.rule: The poster draws a hand (two pair, three of a kind, straight or flush). The first to finish a hand with it, or better, gets 800 from the house.
hand_bounty.cast: The first to make {{hand}} or better gets {{amount}}.
hand_bounty.ribbon: Raymond's count: the first to make {{hand}} or better takes {{amount}}.

eight_aces.name: Ace's aces
eight_aces.rule: The deck gets 8 extra aces (2 of each suit) for the whole match. Repeated cards count, and five of a kind exists, above a straight flush.
eight_aces.cast: 8 extra aces in the deck: five of a kind now counts.
eight_aces.ribbon: Ace's aces: 8 extra aces in the deck.

reveal_one.name: The read
reveal_one.rule: In a drawn hand, one card from each player turns face up for everyone, including one of yours.
reveal_one.cast: One card from each player turns face up.
reveal_one.ribbon: The read: one card from each player is open.

sixth_card.name: One more in the crew
sixth_card.rule: In the first hand to reach the river after the cast, the river brings two cards: the table has six and everyone uses their best 5.
sixth_card.ribbon: One more in the crew: the river brings two cards.

opal.name: The black opal
opal.rule: One card becomes the opal. Whoever wins a pot holding it gets 1,000 from the house. Once only.
opal.cast: This match's opal: {{card}}. Win a pot holding it and get {{amount}}.
opal.ribbon: The black opal: {{card}}. Win a pot with it and get {{amount}}.

tell.name: Le Chiffre's tell
tell.rule: For 3 hands, every oracle bet or raise gives away the tell: bluff when the hand is weak, value when it's good.
tell.cast_one: For {{count}} hand, the oracles' bets give away the tell.
tell.cast_other: For {{count}} hands, the oracles' bets give away the tell.

stack.early_flop: With {{count}} matching, the telegram casts more often and closer together (6 at most).
stack.double_pot: With {{count}} matching, it casts more often. The pot doubles once per hand, never triples.
stack.blackjack: With {{count}} matching, 21 casts more often (500 each).
stack.reveal_one: With {{count}} matching, the read casts more often (always one card per player).
stack.sixth_card: With {{count}} matching, it casts more often. The board never goes past 6 cards.
stack.tell: With {{count}} matching, each cast of the tell lasts more hands (9 at most).
stack.hand_bounty: With {{count}} matching, a new bounty comes after someone claims the last one (3 at most).
stack.opal: With {{count}} matching, a new opal comes after someone claims the last one (3 at most).
stack.eight_aces: Doesn't stack: the deck keeps the same 8 extra aces.
